historical_references.context: A heavy debated topic among Islamic scholars during the time of Imam Al-Shafi'i (767-820 AD) was what constituted the core beliefs (Aqeedah) of Islam. Imam Al-Shafi'i, an influential scholar in Sunan fiqh, compiled and documented the fundamental beliefs of the Muslim community, which became known as Al-Aqeedah Al-Jama'ah (The Collective Creed). The credo emphasized the belief in the Oneness of God, the Prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH), the Angels, the Holy Scriptures, and the Day of Judgment.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Taymiyyah's Aqeedah: The Foundation of His Thought The name Aheedah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In the 13th century, the medieval Islamic scholar Ibn Taymiyyah (1263-1328 AD) is known for having written an influential text on Islamic creed (Aqeedah) entitled Minhaj Al-Sunnah Al-Nabawiyyah (The Methodology of the Prophetic Tradition). In it, he emphasized the need to return to the sources of Islamic knowledge, particularly the Quran and the Hadith, and rejected various deviations from the traditional creed. This work gained significant influence in the Sunni world, especially during the Salafiyya movement of the 19th century.
